_comment: A @Body() that is intentionally left unvalidated, with the reason.
Keyed by controller file -> handler method name. Empty object = exempt nothing.
The only legitimate entries are webhook receivers. Their trust boundary is
an HMAC signature over the RAW body, verified before the payload is read.
Putting a validating DTO in front of one would reject every field the
provider adds later -- a silent integration outage -- and would move the
check from 'is this signed by Shopify' to 'does this match our guess about
Shopify'. The signature is the gate; the shape is not.
An entry that stops matching anything is reported as a stale exemption and
fails the run, exactly like an increase in the count would.
NEVER add a non-webhook handler here. If a body is unvalidated and not
signed by an external provider, it does not belong on this list -- give it

ecommerce/ecommerce.controller.ts.shopifyWebhook: Shopify order webhook. HMAC-SHA256 over req.rawBody verified against the tenant's shared secret before processShopifyOrder sees it. Shopify owns the schema.
ecommerce/ecommerce.controller.ts.woocommerceWebhook: WooCommerce webhook. HMAC verified over req.rawBody against the tenant secret before use. WooCommerce owns the schema.

whatsapp/whatsapp.controller.ts.handleWebhook: Meta Cloud API webhook. x-hub-signature-256 verified over req.rawBody before the payload is read. Meta owns the schema.

paystack/paystack.controller.ts.handleWebhook: Paystack webhook. HMAC-SHA512 over req.rawBody, plus a source-IP allowlist, before the event is dispatched. Paystack owns the schema.
